title: Opposites that strengthen each other: the inclusion of chesed and gevura
overview:
Chapter 22 begins the details of how the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are included in one another. Each *sefira* divides into ten, but in the essence the *din* within *chesed* is still *chesed*; only when the attributes spread out can there be a real *din* in *chesed*.

There are two kinds of *hiskalelus*. In one, opposites nullify each other, as sugar sweetens a lemonade, and this is possible only because each holds its opposite hidden: red food coloring does nothing to a lemon. In the other, the opposite gives strength. *Chesed sheb'gevura* is the strongest *din*: bread to a hungry enemy, reward paid to the wicked in this world. *Gevura sheb'chesed* is the strongest *chesed*: rain in drops, a father's discipline, a cure that leaves one higher than before the blow, which is why He put us into Egypt, and into this world, at all.

All this works because it is a light in a vessel of the opposite kind, like Gavriel, an angel of *gevura* with *chesed* inside. Simple lights, the *Kesarim*, cannot be included, as Beis Hillel and Beis Shammai cannot. Only *mesirus nefesh*, which reaches the Essence, turns even the essence of evil to good.

terms.gloss: inclusion: one attribute included in another, even in its opposite
division; the sefiros divided into ten and ten, where a real din can be in chesed
sweetening; the gevuros sweetened in the chasadim, as sugar in a sour lemonade
strength; what an opposite included in a thing can give it instead of cancelling it
gevura within chesed: a kindness done through din, din in its act and chesed inside, like a father's slap
chesed within gevura: din done through kindness, chesed in its act and din inside, like bread for a hungry enemy
sufferings of love, sent to one who did no bad, to increase his good later
a cure; prepared before the blow, a bitter thing that hurts
the crowns: the simple lights, each entirely separate, which cannot be included in one another
one who returns; in him even the essence of evil turns to good
self-sacrifice; reaches the Essence, above the division of chesed and gevura themselves

sections.title: Every sefira divides into ten, but in its essence each stays what it is
sections.summary: *Chachma* holds a *chesed* and a *gevura* of its own, and each of those holds ten. Yet in the essence the *din* within *chesed* of *chachma* is still *chesed*, and really *chachma*; only when the attributes spread out from the essence can there be a real *din* in *chesed* and *chesed* in *din*.

phrases.he: (כב) ומעתה יש להבין בפרטי התכללות דעשר ספירות דאצילות ותחלה יש לבאר ענין פרטי התחלקות הספירות לי' וי' לי' כו'
כמו חסד שבחכמה שנחלק גם הוא לי', וכהאי גוונא גבורה שבחכמה נחלק לי' כו'.
כי הנה החכמה כלולה מי' היינו כמו חסד וגבורה שבחכמה
phrases.en: In *chachma*, even though in general *chachma* tends to go towards *chesed*, within that whole thing there are really two lines.

phrases.he: להטות כלפי זכות או כלפי חוב

blocks.text: Now come the details of the *hiskalelus* (inclusion) of the ten *sefiros* (Divine attributes) of *Atzilus*, and first how each divides into ten: *chesed* (kindness) within *chachma* (wisdom) divides into ten, and so does *gevura* (might, restraint) within *chachma*. Even though *chachma* in general tends towards *chesed*, within it **there are really two lines**. There is a *gevura* in *chachma* too: to be *medakdek* (exacting) about how things should be, since according to *chachma* it makes sense to make certain *dikdukim* (fine distinctions).

phrases.he: וחסד שבחכמה להטות כלפי זכות, גם הוא כלול מי'
phrases.en: That's also so: the *sefiros* of *chachma* also have *sefiros*.

phrases.he: דהיינו כמו חסד וגבורה שבו לזכות באופן כך וכך,
ולחוב יחייב גם הוא באופן כך וכך
(הגם שהזכות יהפך לחוב בדין שבחכמה,
והחוב יהפך לזכות בחסד שבחכמה,
זהו כאשר הוא בעצם, בלתי התחלקות
phrases.en: That's how it is *b'etzem*, without *hischalkus*.

phrases.he: אבל בהתחלקות
phrases.en: when there is a real *hischalkus*

phrases.he: יוכל להיות גם בחסד שבחכמה בחינת דין ובדין שבחכמה בחינת חסד, כידוע)
phrases.en: At that point from the *sechel* can actually come real *middos*, and from the right can come a real left.

blocks.text: So **the *sefiros* of *chachma* also have *sefiros***. What does it mean that merit turns to guilt by the *din* (judgement) in *chachma*? The *din* in *chesed* of *chachma* is not really a *din*; it is really a *chesed*. It only means that we are going to have a *chesed*, but not such a big one: it puts a limitation on the *chesed*, and it is still a *chesed*.

A *klal gadol* (a great rule): in any *sefira*, all its *sefiros* are really that *sefira*. The *middos* (emotional attributes) of the *sechel* (intellect) are not really *middos*; they are *sechel*. *Chesed* of *chachma* is not a *chesed* at all. When you analyze a situation and conclude that in this instance there should be *chesed*, that is not an actual feeling of love; it is *sechel*. The same the other way: the *sechel* of the *middos* is only their inner part that knows what the thing is, while the real thing is the feeling.

So the *din* of *chesed* in *chachma* is not really *din* but *chesed*, and really not even *chesed* but *chachma*.

That is how it is *b'etzem* (in the essence), without *hischalkus* (division). But **when there is a real *hischalkus***, at that point **from the *sechel* can actually come real *middos*, and from the right can come a real left**. This will be explained.

phrases.he: וכן במדות דחסד וגבורה עצמן, החסד נחלק לי', כח''ב ומדות כו'
דגם שאין מרחמין בדין,
phrases.en: There's a *halacha* that you're not allowed to have *rachamim* in a court case.

phrases.he: היינו בדין העצמי
וכן אין דין בחסד העצמי
phrases.en: Same thing, *b'chesed ha'atzmi* there's no *din*.

phrases.he: אבל בהתפשטותן מן העצם,
phrases.en: when they spread out from the *etzem*

phrases.he: יש חסד בדין ודין בחסד כנזכר לעיל:
phrases.en: Then you can have a *din* in the *chesed* and a *chesed* in a *din*.

blocks.text: So too in the *middos* of *chesed* and *gevura* themselves: the *chesed* divides into ten. There is a *halacha* (law) that you may not have *rachamim* (mercy) in a court case; while working out the *din* you cannot say, "Oh, this poor guy." But that is the essential *din*, and in the same way there is no *din* in the essential *chesed*. **When they spread out from the *etzem***, though, **you can have a *din* in the *chesed* and a *chesed* in a *din***. Now come the kinds of *hiskalelus*.

sections.title: The first inclusion: a thing nullified in its opposite
sections.summary: Opposites can cancel each other, as a reason for guilt overpowers a reason for merit or sugar sweetens lemonade, only because each holds the other hidden within it. Sweet and red have nothing to do with each other, so nothing happens when they meet; sweet and sour together make a taste better than either.

phrases.he: והנה יש התכללות שנקרא ביטול דבר בהיפוכו המנגדו, והיה כמוהו ממש
phrases.en: There's a thing that the two opposites nullify each other.

phrases.he: וכמו מיתוק הגבורות בחסדים כמו שהמקטרג יהפך לסניגור, וכן להיפך שהסניגור יהפך למקטרג
וכמיתוק מים המרים במתוקים
phrases.en: that they overpower

phrases.he: או להיפך

blocks.text: One *hiskalelus* is the *bittul* (nullification) of a thing in its opposite: **the two opposites nullify each other**. So the *misuk* (sweetening) of the *gevuros* in the *chasadim*, the accuser who turns defender and the defender who turns accuser, and the sweet waters that **overpower** the bitter.

phrases.he: וכן ביטול שכל לזכות בשכל לחוב וכהאי גוונא
הרי זה התכללות אמיתי,
phrases.en: That's actually *hiskalelus*.

phrases.he: והיינו רק לפי שיש כח זה במנגד עצמו
phrases.en: Because really there's an *inyan* of *chesed* in that *sechel* of *din*.

phrases.he: ואם לא, לא היה בטל בו

blocks.title: The barefoot child and the future terrorist
blocks.text: So too the *bittul* of a *sechel* for merit in a *sechel* for guilt. The *sechel* of merit sees poor little Palestinian kids without shoes. But the *sechel* of guilt can overpower it totally when it tells you: this is a future terrorist. A listener adds that it is even too much that he has feet, and he answers, "Right, that's the thing."

sensitivity.reason: Takes Palestinian children as the example of a reason for guilt overpowering mercy, calls the child a future terrorist, and keeps a listener's quip that it is too much he has feet.
sensitivity.publishable: So too the *bittul* of a *sechel* for merit in a *sechel* for guilt. The *sechel* of merit sees a poor little child of the enemy without shoes. But the *sechel* of guilt can overpower it totally when it tells you: this is a future terrorist.

blocks.text: **That's actually *hiskalelus***: a *sechel* of *din* can overpower a *sechel* of merit. How is that possible, especially in an *ish chesed* (a man of kindness)? **Because really there's an *inyan* of *chesed* in that *sechel* of *din***. It is not just pure hatred: this one is going to kill Jews, so it is really a *chesed* for Jews.

blocks.title: Arrivals and departures at the airport
blocks.text: Otherwise it would not be nullified in it. As in chapter six, a bitter feeling holds a sweet one and a sweet feeling a bitter one. At the airport there are two meetings: when the uncle or brother comes, everybody is happy; when he goes, everybody is sad. The ones who were happiest at the coming will be saddest at the leaving, because in the sweetness is bitterness, and in the bitterness is sweetness.

Going through the book, you notice that it brings up this theme of opposites over and over. First it asks how opposites can be together, and then it says: that is the whole thing. Being the opposite is what makes it. Sweet and bitter have to do with each other. Sweet and red do not: red is not the opposite of sweet, it has nothing to do with sweet. *Davka* (precisely) the opposite has this thing in it in an opposite way, which means in a hidden way.

blocks.title: Lemonade, sugar and red food coloring
blocks.text: Add sugar to a sour lemonade and they nullify each other, and you come out with a medium taste made of sour and sweet together. But add red food coloring to a lemonade of just lemon and it will not help: it will make it red, and do nothing for the sourness.

phrases.he: כמו במתיקות יש מרירות בהעלם
phrases.en: In the sweetness is bitterness,

phrases.he: ובמרירות יש מתיקות בהעלם
phrases.en: and in the bitterness is sweetness.

phrases.he: כמשל ודמיון מבישול המרקחת מדבש וצנון,
phrases.en: a goodie that they used to make from honey and radish

phrases.he: שנעשה טעם עריבות,
phrases.en: a special good taste that just sweet or just sour wouldn't give you

phrases.he: כולל מחריפות ומתיקות יחד כידוע
phrases.en: sharp and sweet

blocks.title: Honey and radish
blocks.text: The example is **a goodie that they used to make from honey and radish**. It is like sweet and sour: the whole Chinese food is built on this (a listener: the yin and the yang). It makes out of opposite tastes a *taam areivus* (a pleasant taste), **a special good taste that just sweet or just sour wouldn't give you**. Here it is **sharp and sweet**.

phrases.he: וכן יש מטבע האש במים וממים באש
על כן יתכלל אש במים או מים באש כמו שכתוב הוציא מים מאש ואש ממים כו'
וכך במדות חסד וגבורה,
מפני שיש דין בחסד וחסד בדין כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: There's *inyan* of *din* in *chesed* and *chesed* in *din*.

phrases.he: יבוטל הדין בחסד או להיפוך החסד בדין ואם לא, לא היה מתכלל דבר בהיפוכו לעולם

blocks.text: So too there is something of the nature of fire in water and of water in fire, so one can be included in the other: "He brought out water from fire and fire from water." And so with the *middos* of *chesed* and *gevura*: there is *din* in *chesed* and *chesed* in *din*, so one can be nullified in the other. Otherwise nothing would ever be included in its opposite. Like lemon and red: the sweet stays sweet, the red stays red, and there is no *hiskalelus*.

That is one kind of *hiskalelus*: the two do not exactly nullify each other, they actually enhance each other. Taking the edge off each gives an *areivus* (pleasantness) that is more than either. Something super sharp, or just sour like a piece of lemon, you could not even eat, nor plain sugar.

sections.title: The second inclusion: an opposite that gives strength, and chesed sheb'gevura
sections.summary: *Din* can be included in *chesed* not to cancel it but to give it strength, and *chesed* can be the strongest form of *din*: bread for a hungry enemy, the reward He pays the wicked in this world, the prophecy that drove Sancheriv's camp mad.

phrases.he: אמנם הנה יש התכללות מדין בחסד מפני שהוא כמוהו בעצם,
ולא שהוא בטל ממהותו
phrases.en: Not that it'll actually nullify,

phrases.he: אדרבה
phrases.en: just the opposite

phrases.he: נותן בו תוקף ועוז
ועם כל זה נקרא גבורה שבחסד, וכן להיפוך חסד שבגבורה, שנותן כח בגבורה ודין כו'

blocks.text: There is another *hiskalelus* of *din* in *chesed*, because it is like it in its essence. **Not that it'll actually nullify**: **just the opposite**, it gives it *tokef* and *oz* (strength and might). Still it is called *gevura sheb'chesed* (*gevura* within *chesed*), and the other way round *chesed sheb'gevura*, which gives strength to *gevura* and *din*.

phrases.he: והענין הוא כידוע, על דרך אם רעב שונאך האכילהו לחם, כי גחלים כו'
הרי בחסד וטוב זה עושה לו רעה ודין גמור לאבד נפשו
וכן משלם לשונאיו כדי להאבידו,
phrases.en: He pays his enemy upfront, in order to destroy him.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא כל בחינת דין ועונש שנעשה בבחינת חסד

blocks.title: Bread for a hungry enemy
blocks.text: "If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread, for coals..." He never knew exactly how to apply this until someone in the class told him about a certain person. The plainer meaning: a man who is your enemy has become poor, and you go and give him a buck: "Here buddy, buy yourself something to eat." Getting it from his enemy hurts him even more. He has to take it, because he is hungry, but while he eats the bread it feels like he is eating coals. In this kindness is the full strength of *din*, to destroy him.

So too He pays His enemies in this world. The *Aibershter* (G-d) never withholds anyone's reward: *din* means justice, and He pays for any small thing. But He pays *davka* in this world. That is why evil people sometimes have a good time here: everybody did something good here and there, and He is paying them off. As the verse says, "He repays His enemies to their face, to destroy them": **He pays his enemy upfront**, where it does not count, so that later, when it counts, there is nothing left to pay him. Then He can fix him good.

phrases.he: הרי הוא עוז ותוקף הדין ביותר, ונקרא חסד שבגבורה
וכמו והשמיע יהו״ה את הוד קולו במחנה סנחרב

blocks.text: That is the greatest strength of *din*, and it is called *chesed sheb'gevura*. So with the camp of Sancheriv. He is not sure of the verse, but later the text says He sent the angel of *Havaya*. What did it do for them? It gave them something people hope for: it let them hear what is going on upstairs, a *shtikel nevua* (a bit of prophecy). But they were not ready for it, so it totally blew their minds and they started killing each other.

sections.title: Gevura sheb'chesed: kindness made stronger by restraint, and the blow before the cure
sections.summary: A kindness done through *din* is stronger than plain kindness: rain in drops, a contracted light, the sufferings of love, a father's discipline. He prepares the cure before the blow, and strikes at all because the cure leaves a person higher than before, as Egypt, the exile and this whole world do.

phrases.he: וכן להיפוך בבחינת גבורה שבחסד, שהמעשה של חסד עשוי במדת הדין
להיות בו יותר תוקף ועוז
phrases.en: Then it's even stronger.

phrases.he: כמו גבורות גשמים, שבאים בצמצום
phrases.en: The *geshamim* have to come *davka* in droplets,

phrases.he: כדי שיומשך בריבוי
phrases.en: in order that you should have a lot of rain.

phrases.he: וכמו צמצום אור השפע בכל מקום, כדי שיתקבל
phrases.en: The *mashpia* has to be *metzamtzem* the *or hashefa* in order that the *mekabel* will be able to get it.

blocks.text: And the other way, *gevura sheb'chesed*: the act of *chesed* is done with the attribute of *din*, and **then it's even stronger**. So the rains: the *geshamim* (rains) **have to come *davka* in droplets**, so that there is a lot of rain; in a torrent they would destroy things. And as learned earlier, the *mashpia* (giver) has to *metzamtzem* (contract) the light of the flow so that the *mekabel* (receiver) is able to get it.

phrases.he: וכן התחלקות ע''ב גשרים כו',
וכן יסורים של אהבה,
וכאב את בן ירצה, מייסרו
phrases.en: If the father loves his son, then he will discipline him.

blocks.text: So too the division into seventy-two bridges. It is explained in a certain place that in *chachma* there are 72 synapses, 72 connections, between the 72 Names or something like that. The connection is not made as if it were all one thing: they are separate things with little narrow bridges between them, and this makes it bigger and better.

*Yissurim shel ahava* (sufferings of love) are the opposite of paying the wicked in this life for their good: they pay good people in this life for whatever little bad they did. And really they are even more than that. They come when he did no bad at all, and still the *Aibershter* sends him suffering, to increase even the good He will give him later. As "the father the son he favors": **if the father loves his son, then he will discipline him**.

phrases.he: שהחסד נעשה בלבוש דמדת הדין דווקא
phrases.en: The *chesed* is done in an enclothment of *din*.

phrases.he: והרי זה דווקא תוקף החסד יותר מעצם החסד

blocks.text: **The *chesed* is done in an enclothment of *din***, and that is *davka* more the strength of *chesed* than *chesed* itself. A father who disciplines his son proves his love more than a father who is always nice to him.

phrases.he: וכמו הקדים רפואה למכה,
phrases.en: Before He even hit him, He already had the *refua* ready.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב כי הוא יך וירפאנו
ולכאורה למה צריך להכאה כלל?
phrases.en: Why should he have hit you?

phrases.he: אך על ידי הרפואה יברא ויתחזק יותר

blocks.text: "He prepared the cure before the blow," as "He wounds and He heals": before He even struck, **He already had the *refua* ready**. But this is a very big question: why strike at all? Why does He make this weird world?

blocks.title: He took us out of Egypt? He put us there!
blocks.text: The whole world is made this weird way. We thank the *Aibershter* for taking us out of Egypt. What do you mean? He put us into Egypt! It is like pushing someone into a ditch, pulling him out and telling him, "You owe me one, ain't I a nice guy?" You would call the cops on him for pushing you in. Isn't that exactly what the *Aibershter* is doing? As we are reading now, Yosef went down to Egypt; later He says make a *Pesach*, eat *matzos*, say the *Haggada*, and we thank Him so much for taking us out, after we suffered there terribly, 400 years (or 210, as a listener asks: the 400 count from the covenant between the parts).

blocks.title: From the high roof to the deep pit
blocks.text: Really the question goes on the whole world. We are in the world; we will learn Torah and go up to spiritual levels, to heaven. Wait a minute: we were higher than heaven! "From a high roof to a deep pit": we were living in a high palace and You pushed us into this low pit, and now You will send *Moshiach* to pull us out? That is the basic question in "He wounds and He heals."

blocks.question: Does the *Haggada* not mention that He put us into Egypt?
blocks.text: It does, but not as a bad thing. It tells it as praise: as He told Avraham at the covenant between the parts, "Know that your seed will be strangers in a land not theirs," and Yaakov went down by the word of G-d. One would think it should not be a praise: if someone punches you and then fixes it up, you are not happy that he bandaged your boo-boo.

**Why should he have hit you?** Because through the cure he is refined and strengthened more. That is the whole idea of *yerida l'tzorech aliya* (a descent for the sake of an ascent): the world was not created just so that we should end up where we started.

blocks.title: Exercise makes you sore
blocks.text: A listener says it is the idea of a vaccine. It is also the idea of exercise, which actually destroys your muscles and makes you sore. So you complain: I wasn't feeling all that great, I was fat and flabby, and now you made me exercise and I'm sore all over, I can hardly move. But he is going to come out higher than the original.

When they came out of Egypt, they went from the level of *Bnei Noach* (the children of Noah) to the level of Israel. And the whole *golus* (exile) of the world, from its beginning until now, started with the Tree of Knowledge: we went into *golus* at the level of Adam, which is *chaya*, and we will come out at the level of *Moshiach*, which is *yechida*. People say He is "awesome in His plot against men": He knew it would happen, it was a setup, so what if He helps now; He should not have set us up in the first place. The reason is that it is going to be better.

phrases.he: כי החולה הוא בחינת הדין הקשה, ויעובר על ידי מידת הדין שבחסד, שהוא הרפואה מדברים קשים כו'
וכהאי גוונא בכל מיתוק הדין, בשרשו דווקא, היינו בדין שבחסד דווקא להיותו תוקפו של חסד, לגבור על הדין ולהמתיקו כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: Illness is the harsh *din*, and the cure comes from hard things. Medicine too is a bitter, hard thing; in fact it is something a healthy person should not take. So with every sweetening of *din*: it is *davka* at its root, in the *din* within *chesed*, the *tokef* (strength) of *chesed* that overpowers the *din* and sweetens it. This is the *tokef* of *chesed* and the *tokef* of *din*.

sections.title: Both at once: each holds two opposites, as Gavriel saved Avraham
sections.summary: *Gevura sheb'chesed* and *chesed sheb'gevura* are even greater opposites than *chesed* and *gevura*, yet they can come together because each acts for the sake of its opposite: a slap that is love, a raise that is ruin. So Gavriel, an angel of *gevura*, saved Avraham with a light of *chesed* inside him.

phrases.he: ובכל זה יובן איכות אופני פרטי ההתכללות דחסד וגבורה, כמו גם גבורה שבחסד עם חסד שבגבורה
דגם שהן ב' הפכים ביותר, שזה תוקף החסד וזה תוקף בגבורה
ומכל שכן מצד התפשטות לבושים מחולפים, שזה פועל דין וזה פועל חסד
phrases.en: Even more so because of the spreading out of the opposite *levushim*, that this one actually does a *din*, and this one actually does a *chesed*.

phrases.he: אבל מכל מקום
phrases.en: But nonetheless

phrases.he: מצד שכל אחד פועל בשביל דבר היפוכו דוקא,
שגבורה שבחסד פעולתו דין ופנימיותו חסד,
וחסד שבגבורה פעולתו חסד ופנימיותו דין,
על כן יוכלו לבוא כאחד דוקא, מפני שכל אחד מראה ב' הפכים על כל פנים
phrases.en: Nonetheless, each one of them has two opposites in it.

blocks.text: From all this the details of the *hiskalelus* of *chesed* and *gevura* are understood, even of *gevura sheb'chesed* with *chesed sheb'gevura*. These are even bigger opposites than *chesed* and *gevura* themselves: one is the *tokef* of *chesed*, the other the *tokef* of *gevura*. And the text does not mean "in spite of", he corrects himself: it is even more so, because of the opposite *levushim* (garments) they spread into, one doing *din* and one doing *chesed*.

**But nonetheless**, since each acts for the sake of its opposite, they can come as one. *Gevura sheb'chesed* is *din* in its act and *chesed* inside: a father slaps his son, but inside he is trying to grow him up good. *Chesed sheb'gevura* is *chesed* in its act, like giving someone a raise, and *din* inside: really he is messing him up. **Each one of them has two opposites in it**.

phrases.he: וכמו גבריאל שהציל לאברהם, וכן צינן את הגחלים
הרי זה מבחינת גבורה שבחסד
phrases.en: So it was Gavriel, but it was *gevura sheb'chesed*.

blocks.text: Gavriel saved Avraham and cooled the coals. It seems backwards: Gavriel is the angel of *din*. **So it was Gavriel, but it was *gevura sheb'chesed***. But *chesed* is *chesed*; how is Gavriel *gevura sheb'chesed*? Because he is an angel, and an angel is a *levush*, a *kli* (vessel), not a light. *Gevura sheb'chesed* means that the light, the *sefira*, is *chesed*... (here the side ends).

The next side picks up the point. That is what "an angel of G-d" means: the Name is in him. The angel is the *kli*, the Name is inside, and he is its *levush*; different Names, of the right side and of the left, go into the angels. He read recently, he thinks in *Tanya*, in *Shaar HaYichud v'HaEmuna*, though he is not sure, that when an angel is on a *shlichus* (mission) the Name is in him to the point that the angel is called G-d: "I saw G-d." When he is not on a mission he says "*kadosh*, *kadosh*, *kadosh*": separate. A listener recalls Rashi on Esav's angel, a few portions back: angels on a mission are called by the Name *Elokim*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 034 opens by finishing the point on Gavriel (line 51) where the previous side stopped, and only then rereads line 51 (w328).

blocks.text: So the angel was the angel of *gevura*, because the act was *gevura*: *gevura sheb'chesed*. But the inside was *chesed*: the Name in him was *chesed*.
blocks.outOfPlace: The end of the opening on Gavriel and the rereading of line 51 (w328-332), before line 52.

phrases.he: כמו זיעה טובה מוציא את חולי החום,
וכרפואה למכה כו'
phrases.en: the *refua* is a bitter thing, it hurts

phrases.he: והוא המכה במחנה סנחרב בבחינת חסד שבגבורה,
כמו שכתוב ויצא מלאך יהו״ה כו'
phrases.en: It was a *malach Havaya* that came out.

blocks.title: Sweating out a fever
blocks.text: A good sweat drives out the illness of the fever. If someone has a fever and you want to cool him down, what you actually have to do is heat him up: cover him with blankets; do not put him outside to cool off; make him sweat. Because the cure is a blow: **the *refua* is a bitter thing, it hurts**.

sensitivity.reason: Tells how to treat a fever (cover him with blankets, make him sweat, do not cool him off), which a reader might act on.
sensitivity.publishable: A good sweat drives out the illness of the fever: to cool the fever, the sick man is heated up and made to sweat. Because the cure is a blow: **the *refua* is a bitter thing, it hurts**.

blocks.text: And that is the blow to Sancheriv's camp, from *chesed sheb'gevura*, as it says, "An angel of *Havaya* went out." What did he do? He gave them a big *chesed*: he let them see, and hear, upstairs.

sections.title: Light and vessel: why the opposites are no contradiction
sections.summary: The inclusion is a light of *chesed* in a vessel of *gevura*, which acts opposite to its light, and the reverse. Light and vessel are like form and matter, so there is no contradiction; the lights themselves, the intentions, cannot be included.

phrases.he: והיינו לאכללא שמאלא בימינא וימינא בשמאלא שהוא כמו אור החסד בכלי הגבורה, שפועל הכלי היפך האור שלו שכלי הגבורה פועל דין, היפוך אור של חסד שבו
וכן להיפוך, כלי החסד פועל חסד,
היפוך אור הגבורה שבו
phrases.en: The *or*, the actual intention, is opposite.

phrases.he: ואין זה היפך כלל, מאחר שהוא בבחינת אור וכלי,
phrases.en: And it's not really opposite, because that's an *or* and *kli*.

phrases.he: שהוא כענין חומר וצורה (כמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: This is to include the left in the right and the right in the left: like the light of *chesed* in the vessel of *gevura*, where the vessel does *din*, opposite to its own light. And the other way, the vessel of *chesed*, like the one giving the raise, does *chesed*, while the light, the actual intention, is the opposite.

**And it's not really opposite, because that's an *or* and *kli***, a light and a vessel, which is like matter and form, as will be explained. The actual lights, though, cannot really be included: the intention of *chesed* is opposite to the intention of *din*, and you cannot combine them.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין התכללות דשם מ''ב ושם ע''ב, שהן ב' פרשיות דקריאת שמע כו'

blocks.text: Elsewhere the *hiskalelus* of the Name of forty-two and the Name of seventy-two is explained: they are the two paragraphs of the *Shema*. Did anyone ever count them properly? A student had. The second paragraph is not really 72 words: there are more, but up to a certain point it is 72, because the paragraph as counted there is shorter than the one we read. Count all the words and count the repeated words twice, and it comes out as stated there. He does not remember what number was given, "but, yeah, it works."

phrases.he: וכמו עקידת יצחק באברהם, איש החסד
וכתנופת הלוים, שנכללו בחסדים דכהנים
phrases.en: that they were given to serve the *kohanim*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב וילוו עליך ואיך ישרת את היפוכו?
וכהאי גוונא רבים
phrases.en: There's many instances like this.

blocks.text: So with Avraham, who is *chesed*, and the waving of the Levites, who are a matter of *gevura*, included in the *chasadim* of the priests: **they were given to serve the *kohanim***. "They shall join you and serve you": how can one serve its opposite? **There's many instances like this**.

sections.title: Only where there is division: vessels can be included, simple lights cannot
sections.summary: Opposites include each other only because each has divided and holds something of the other, as the angels, which are vessels, do, and as *Tikkun*, with its many vessels, allows. The simple lights, the *Kesarim*, cannot be included at all, as the depth of good and the depth of evil cannot, or the essential opinions of Beis Hillel and Beis Shammai.

phrases.he: וכל זה אינו רק מצד בחינת ההתחלקות שבכל אחד
על כן מצא מין את מינו וניעור,
phrases.en: and it wakes it up

phrases.he: גם בהיותם ב' הפכים ממש כו'
phrases.en: even though they're totally *hafuchim*

phrases.he: וכמו ענין התחלקות מיכאל וגבריאל, שר של אש ומים ואין מכבין זה את זה, כמו שכתוב עושה השלום כו' לפי שיש בכל אחד מהיפוכו המנגדו דוקא

blocks.text: All this is only because of the division in each one. So kind finds kind **and it wakes it up**, **even though they're totally *hafuchim*** (opposites). So Michael and Gavriel, the angel of fire and the angel of water, do not put each other out: "He makes peace." But this is *davka* by the angels, which are vessels, because each has something of its opposite in it.

That is why *Tikkun* (the world of Repair) has few lights and many vessels. *Tohu* (the world of Chaos) has big lights, so the guy cannot give up his position: it is about the essence of the principle, and he cannot move to the opposite one. But a vessel of *gevura* can take in a light of *chesed*: from the vessels there can be a *hispaalus*.

phrases.he: אבל באורות הפשוטים בתכלית, כמו בחינת הנקודות הנקרא כתרים,
אי אפשר להם להתכלל כלל
phrases.en: they can't join

phrases.he: מפני שכל אחד נבדל לגמרי מזולתו, ולא ימצא בו כלל מבחינת המנגדו כמו עצם בחינת הטוב שבעצמיות נפש איש הטוב, הנקרא עומק טוב, עם עצם הרע, הנקרא עומק רע כו'

blocks.text: But the simple lights, the points called *Kesarim* (crowns), as explained before with *Akudim*, *Nekudim* and *Berudim*: **they can't join**, because each is entirely separate from the other and has nothing in it of its opposite. Like the essence of good in the soul of a good man, called the depth of good, and the essence of evil, called the depth of evil.

Like the essence of good of a Rebbe and, *l'havdil* (to distinguish them), a Nazi, may his name be blotted out. And so with the essence of a principle, even in the intellect: in the essence of their reasoning, Beis Hillel and Beis Shammai cannot join. Only in the spreading out, in the vessels, can they join. The opinion of Beis Shammai is still the same as it was then: the actual opinion in the essence of the intellect did not change.

sections.title: Higher than division: the baal teshuva and mesirus nefesh
sections.summary: Yet a *baal teshuva* turns even the essence of evil to good, because *mesirus nefesh* reaches the Essence, above the division of *chesed* and *gevura* themselves. From there one can ask for a change of will in essence, and "*Havaya* passed before him" turns even essential *din* to *chesed*.

phrases.he: אך בבעלי תשובה אנו רואים שנהפך גם עצם הרע לטוב,
phrases.en: But in a *baal teshuva* it could change.

phrases.he: וכן זדונות עצמן נעשו כזכיות הרי הוא מצד מסירת נפש בעצמות אור אין סוף, שלמעלה גם מהתחלקות עצם החסד וגבורה

blocks.text: Yet **in a *baal teshuva* it could change**: even the essence of evil turns to good. The *Kesarim* are the essence, the *etzem haratzon* (essence of the will), as was explained about *Tohu*. So intentional sins become as merits, and not only as merits: they can actually become merits. That is from *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) in the Essence of the *Ein Sof*, above even the division of the essential *chesed* and *gevura*: higher than the *Kesarim*, in the actual *hiyuli*. From up there even the lights can be included.

phrases.he: ולכך יכולים במסירת נפש דווקא, להתפלל ולומר יהי רצון, בעצם, מלפניך כו'
וכן ויעבור יהו״ה על פניו כו'
phrases.en: The *Aibershter* went past the *pnimiyus*; He went past even the *pnimiyus* of the *ratzonos*.

phrases.he: אל רחום, להפוך גם הדין בעצם לחסד כו', וכמו שיתבאר בענין י''ג תקוני דיקנא כו' ודי למבין

blocks.text: So with *mesirus nefesh*, *davka*, one can say "May it be Your will" in essence, from before You. And so "*Havaya* passed before him": **The *Aibershter* went past the *pnimiyus***, the inner aspect, even of the wills, "G-d, merciful", to turn even the essential *din* to *chesed*. The text says this will be explained with the thirteen *tikkunei dikna* (features of the beard); he is not sure where, since he does not see anywhere in the book that it explains them.

phrases.he: (והיינו על ידי בחינת הקו וחוט, שיש בו מכח עצמות אור אין סוף ממש
כמו שכתוב זכרונם לברכה אליו ולא למדותיו, גם לא למדותיו העצמיים כו'
phrases.en: To Him and not His *middos*, meaning from higher than even the *middos ha'atzmiyim*.

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר בעזרת השם ודי למבין):

blocks.text: This is higher than the division and higher than the receiving itself: it has the power of the Essence of the *Ein Sof* *mamash* (literally). There, below, it is all a matter of actions, and this is higher still, as our sages said: to Him and not to His attributes, meaning from higher than even the essential attributes.

blocks.question: The text speaks of the thirteen attributes of mercy but does not really explain them; of those it does, it only tells about "bearing iniquity" and "clearing". What about the other eleven?
blocks.text: He does explain the source: why they are thirteen attributes of mercy, as later in chapters 25 and 26: *davka* because they are higher than the *chachma* of *Arich*, higher than the division of the laws of the *mitzvos*. What the other eleven are and why thirteen, he does not spell out. He explains it, but you have to figure it out.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the *din* within *chesed* of *chachma* not really *din*, and when can there be a real *din* in *chesed*?
Why can sugar change a lemonade when red food coloring cannot, and what does this say about opposites?
How is feeding a hungry enemy, or paying the wicked in this world, *chesed sheb'gevura*?
If He prepared the cure before the blow, why strike at all? How does this answer "He put us into Egypt"?
How could Gavriel, the angel of *gevura*, save Avraham by *gevura sheb'chesed*?
Why can the *Kesarim* not be included in one another, and how does a *baal teshuva* change even the essence of evil?

notes.text: 033 w316-353: he gives the example as "שכל שבבינה" (an analysis that concludes there should be chesed), probably meaning a chesed of bina or of the intellect; the block does not name the sefira.

033 w793-808: "that's even too much that he has feet" is probably a listener's quip (no speaker labels); his "Right, that's the thing" may only be an acknowledgement. The block says so; the flag asks the reviewer to weigh it.
Line 38: he reads קשרים (connections) for the text's גשרים (bridges) and speaks of 72 "synapses", "between the 72 names or something like that", from "a certain place" he does not name.

Lines 42-43: he reads יבורר for יברא, and "והוא בא על ידי מדת הרחמים שבחסד" for "ויעובר על ידי מידת הדין שבחסד" (033 w3624-3640). The block follows the text's sense (the cure from hard things, din within chesed) as he goes on to explain it.

033 w1667-1690 and w3926-3952: he says a student told him about a certain person, which taught him how to apply "feed your enemy bread", and later gives chesed sheb'gevura as "with the Persians... he gave him a raise, but really he's messing him up" (034 w508-526: "like the person that's giving the raise"). The reference is not explained on the tape; the blocks keep the raise and leave out "the Persians".

Side 1 (033) stops mid-sentence at w4069 ("the Name Havaya of"); side 2 (034) opens with "I can't remember where I read this", so a little may be lost between the sides. 034 has Sofer word times, not re-timed ones.

034 w86-287: he is unsure where he read that an angel on a mission is called G-d ("I think it's in Tanya... I think it's Shaar HaYichud v'HaEmuna. I'm not sure"); a listener ties it to Rashi on Esav's angel. Left as said.
034 w495-507: after "the vessel of gevura does din" he says "like a pot"; unclear, left out.

034 w594-810: the count of words in the two paragraphs of the Shema is a back-and-forth with a student, partly unclear ("ויולך etc. twice", "השם אלוקיכם אמת twice"); the aside keeps only that counting the repeated words twice makes it come out.
Line 60: the transcript has only "באברהם איז א חסד" (034 w818-821); the block does not mention the binding of Yitzchak, which he does not discuss.
Line 76: he reads "היינו זה בחינת התקבלו" for "והיינו על ידי בחינת הקו וחוט" (034 w1401-1417), so the block does not mention the Kav.

Line 75 and the last question: he says he does not find where the book explains the thirteen tikkunei dikna (034 w1373-1398); the closing exchange (w1484-1655) has no speaker labels, so who says what is inferred.
